manifest.name: @ilaomianyang/dsh-memory-graph
manifest.author: ISKING <admin@isking.cc>
manifest.description: Long-term associative memory for DeepSeek Harness: a local plain-text vault of raw episodes, typed memory cards and entity pages, configured from 设置 → 记忆图谱, and a Memory tab inside a conversation that draws what that session remembered. No build step; the only dependency is the harness's own schema library, used for the Settings page.

scripts.test: node test/smoke.mjs && node test/schema.mjs && node test/client.mjs && node test/capture.mjs && node test/tools.mjs && node test/extract.mjs && node test/graphdata.mjs && node test/page.mjs && node test/distillapi.mjs && node test/auto.m...
scripts.release: npm version patch -m "chore(release): v%s" && git push --follow-tags

bundle.text:
- insert:
    - id: memory-graph
      name: '@ilaomianyang/dsh-memory-graph'
      config:
        vaultDir: ''
        capture:
          enabled: true
        extractor:
          enabled: false
          # harness = borrow the provider / model / thinking level selected in
          # Settings → Models (no key needed). Switch to 'http' to post to your
          # own OpenAI-compatible endpoint with baseUrl + apiKeyEnv instead.
          transport: 'harness'

readme.text:
[English](README.en.md) · 中文

[](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@ilaomianyang/dsh-memory-graph) [](https://github.com/ilaomianyang/dsh-memory-graph/actions/workflows/test.yml)

给 DeepSeek Harness 的**长期联想记忆**插件。上下文压缩会把东西真的抹掉；这个插件在上下文之外留一层持久的、可读的、属于你自己的记忆。

配置在 **设置 → 记忆图谱** 里，一页四组，改完即生效；看的时候有三个地方——**会话页签里的「记忆」**画出这个会话记住了什么，记忆库根目录的 graph.html 画出整个库，**左侧栏的「记忆图谱」**把同一张整库图直接搬进应用里。

纯 Node ESM，不需要构建。唯一的运行依赖是 Harness 自带的 `@deepseek-ai/schemastery`——它提供配置的 schema，设置页读的就是它投影出来的那份值；没装这个依赖时插件照常跑，只是「记忆图谱」这一页不会出现在侧栏。

---

readme.section: 它和"压缩上下文"有什么不同
readme.text:
| | 上下文压缩 | 本插件 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 目的 | 让当前对话塞得进窗口 | 让三个月前的决定还能被找回 |
| 丢失 | 压掉就是没了 | 原始事件永不被改写，只追加 |
| 结构 | 一段摘要 | 带类型、带时间、带来源的卡片 + 实体连接 |
| 变化 | 不可见 | 冲突变成 supersede 链，"怎么变成现在这样"可读 |
| 位置 | 会话日志内部 | 独立文件夹，可移植、可直接读 |

一句话：**压缩是工作记忆策略，这个插件是长期记忆。两者不是替代关系，是并存的。**

```
episodes/   原始层  每轮追加一行 JSON，不蒸馏、不删除           ← 保证"不会消失"
cards/      语义层  从原始层蒸馏出的带类型记忆卡片（markdown）  ← 真正的检索对象
entities/   索引层  每个东西一页，带提及时间线                  ← 跨项目联想的桥
```

模型检索的时候，走的是 `cards + entities`；`episodes` 是蒸馏的原料，也是出事时的对账依据。

```markdown
---
id: "c-20261102-7f3a"
kind: "decision"
title: "记忆存储用纯文本文件而不是 SQLite"

`status` 只会是 `active` / `superseded` / `retracted`。**被推翻的记忆不会被删掉**，它变成 `superseded` 并指向新卡片——这正是"事物的发展"能被读出来的原因。

**从 npm 装**（不用碰 GitHub）：

```
plugin_manager action=install_bundle target="@ilaomianyang/dsh-memory-graph"
```

pnpm 会把唯一的依赖 `@deepseek-ai/schemastery` 一起装好。国内装不动的话，给 `install_bundle` 加 `registry="https://registry.npmmirror.com/"`——npmmirror 会自动同步 npm 上的版本，通常是发布后几分钟到几小时。

**从源码装**（想跟着改的时候）：

```
git clone https://github.com/ilaomianyang/dsh-memory-graph
cd dsh-memory-graph
npm install                 # 只有一个依赖，Harness 自带的 schema 库
```

然后在 Harness 里让模型执行，或者自己在插件管理里填那个目录的绝对路径：

```
plugin_manager action=install_bundle target="<clone 下来的绝对路径>"
```

这条路 `install_bundle` 用 `link:` 方式装本地目录，**不会**替你装依赖，所以上面那步 `npm install` 别跳过。不装也能用，只是设置里看不到那一页。

想跟着改：`git pull` 之后重载插件即可（`plugin_manager action=set_plugin target="include:memory-graph" enabled=false`，再 `enabled=true`）。

**装完要重启一次 Harness**（关掉窗口重开）。原因不是偷懒：Web 侧的插件清单是启动时扫一遍运行中的 loader 条目、读各自 `package.json` 的 `dsh.client` 字段定下的，这份扫描结果在进程里有缓存，之后不会再读第二遍。所以新装、或者改了 `client.js` / `package.json`，都得让进程重来一次；装完不重启，侧栏里不会有「记忆图谱」，而你手上不会有任何报错提示。

重启后打开 **设置 → 记忆图谱**（在「模型」和「内置插件」之间）。卸载：`plugin_manager action=remove_bundle target="@ilaomianyang/dsh-memory-graph"`。**记忆库不会被删**，它在 `~/dsh-memory`，独立于插件。

从 npm 装的那份，设置页最上面有「版本与更新」一行：当前版本号、**检查更新**、**立即更新**。

上面这张是真机（开发机上是 `link:` 安装，所以「更新」是灰的，旁边就写着原因）：版本号、是否最新、用的哪个源、上次检查时间，下面四个开关是 `update.*`。

- 插件启动时自己查一次，之后每 `update.checkEveryHours` 小时（默认 12）最多查一次。查的是 `<注册表>/@ilaomianyang%2fdsh-memory-graph/latest`——一次 GET，不带查询串、不带你的记忆库路径、不带任何对话内容。结果记在库里的 `.update-state.json`，离线时保留上一次的答案，不会把"查不到"显示成"已是最新"。
- 点「立即更新」才装。安装走宿主自己的 `pluginManager.installBundle`，和 `dsh plugin` / 插件管理里那条路是同一条，尊重你配的 registry，不再造第二个包管理器。
- **`link:` 本地安装会拒绝更新**，不是报错，是明说："这会覆盖你的开发目录"。从源码装的那份，更新就是 `git pull` + 重载插件，见上一节。
- 装完通常要重启 Harness 才生效（和 `client.js` / `package.json` 同一类原因）。页面会直接写「需要重启 Harness 生效」，不会假装已经好了。
- `update.autoInstall`（默认关）：启动时发现新版本就自己装，不用点。它在任何对话开始之前动手，是唯一"换掉插件不会打断你正在说的话"的时刻。`link:` 安装同样拒绝。
- `memory_stats` 也会报一行版本，模型想知道自己手上是哪一版时不用猜。
不想让它联网就把 `update.enabled` 关掉：那之后一次请求都不发，页面只显示当前版本。

```
~/dsh-memory/
├── vault.json                     库的元信息（schema 版本、创建时间）
├── projects.json                  见到过的项目 slug
├── README.md                      自动生成的目录页，链接到每张卡片

纯文本、一文件一记忆、只追加不重写——可以 `git init` 自己版本化，或者直接 `grep -r` 全库搜索。这是本地私有数据，只属于你一个人；共享出去的是这个插件项目，不是记忆库。

**设置 → 记忆图谱**。这个插件在 Settings 的侧栏里自带一页，四组：采集 / 隐私 / 抽取器 / 检索。每项都有中英文说明，改完按「保存」即时生效，不用重启、不用重载。

- 改过的字段带「已改」标记，点旁边的「恢复默认」退回默认值（不是清空成空串）。
- 保存被拒会直接说原因（数字越界、宿主刚被别处改过），不会悄悄吞掉。
- 抽取器那一组跟着你选的路线走：`transport` 选 `harness` 只看模型相关的几项，选 `http` 才出现 endpoint / key。

**四个不在这页上的键**：总开关 `enabled`、记忆库目录 `vaultDir`、默认项目名 `defaultProject`、跨项目连接 `crossProject`。它们在插件启动时就被读掉了（决定库在哪、按哪个项目归档、要不要连跨项目实体），改它们要重载插件，所以留在 profile 的 `cordis.patch.yml` 里手写。同一行的 `config` 下也能写页面上的那些项——**YAML 是最终事实**，两边改都行：

| 键 | 默认 | 说明 | 在设置页 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | `true` | 总开关，关掉就是彻底不加载 | — |
| `vaultDir` | `~/dsh-memory` | 记忆库位置，支持 `~` | — |
| `defaultProject` | `shared` | 会话没有 cwd 时归档到哪个项目 | — |
| `crossProject` | `true` | 新卡片是否连进项目实体枢纽 | — |
| `capture.enabled` | `true` | 是否自动追加原始事件 | ✓ |
| `capture.userChars` | `1500` | 你每条消息最多存多少字，超出截断 | ✓ |
| `capture.assistantChars` | `1500` | 助手每条回复最多存多少字 | ✓ |
| `capture.includeToolOutput` | `false` | 是否记录工具名与调用次数（**不记录内容**） | ✓ |

为什么只有这 41 个能在这页改？Harness 的设置机制只投影**声明为 volatile 的字段**，也就是"每次用到时才读"的那些。上面带 ✓ 的都是这种：改一次，下一次调用就换了。而 `enabled` / `vaultDir` / `defaultProject` / `crossProject` 是在激活时消费的，改了得重载插件，所以不放进页面装样子——页面底部会直接把这件事写出来，而不是给你几个点了没反应的开关。

readme.section: 什么时候它会自己蒸：三条规则
readme.text:
默认**不自动**。打开 `auto.enabled` 之后，插件每分钟看一次「现在该不该蒸」——这一眼只做算术（未蒸馏条数、距上次多久、是不是静默时段），**不调模型、不花钱**。命中规则才真的跑一次，跑的还是同一个 `distill()`。

三条规则互相独立，可以只开一条，也可以都开：

| 规则 | 配置 | 什么时候触发 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 攒够就蒸 | `auto.minEpisodes` | 未蒸馏情节 ≥ 这个数（比如 10 条） |
| 定时蒸 | `auto.everyMinutes` | 距上次自动蒸馏 ≥ 这么多分钟（1440 = 每天一次） |
| 追平 | `auto.catchUp` | 还攒着**一整批**（≥ `maxEpisodesPerRun` 条）时就一批批蒸下去，每批之间隔 `auto.catchUpEveryMinutes`（默认 10），一天最多 `auto.maxBatchesPerDay` 批（默认 6，0 = 不限） |

readme.section: 什么时候它会自己蒸：三条规则
readme.text:
「追平」是给**积压**用的：导入了历史会话、或者一周没开机回来，未蒸馏的可能有两千条——前两条规则一次只消化一批，靠它们要等几十天。打开追平，它会自己一批批往前推，直到剩下不到一整批为止，然后安安静静等下一次。

- 它**自己**有节奏（`catchUpEveryMinutes`），不受 `minGapMinutes` 限制；另外两条规则仍然受。
- `maxBatchesPerDay` 是唯一给自动花钱**设上限**的旋钮：默认 6 批 ≈ 240 条情节/天。想快点追平就调大，不想它半夜跑就把 `quietHours` 设上。
- 追平跑到一半被打断（重启、关机、锁被别人拿着）没关系：计数在 `.auto-state.json` 里，第二天（或下一个间隔）继续，已经蒸过的不会重蒸。
- 2080 条积压 + 默认配置：6 批/天 × 40 条 ≈ 9 天追平；想一天追完就把上限调到 50。

另外三个闸门，规则之间共用：

readme.section: 什么时候它会自己蒸：三条规则
readme.text:
- `auto.minGapMinutes`（默认 30）：两条**非追平**规则共用：两次自动蒸馏至少隔这么久。它先于那两条规则判断——刚攒够就被反复问是没意义的，而且每次问都要花钱。
- `auto.quietHours`（默认空）：这段时间里不跑，可以跨午夜（`23:00-08:00`）。写不对就当没写，不会因此永远不跑。追平也听它。
- `auto.project`（默认空）：自动蒸出来的卡片记到哪个项目；留空用最近那条情节的项目。

几个刻意的选择：

readme.section: 什么时候它会自己蒸：三条规则
readme.text:
- **定时蒸的时钟从打开那一刻算起**：刚打开不会立刻跑一次——「每天一次」不该在你按下开关的瞬间就花掉一次调用。时钟单独存（`startedAt`），不当作"上次运行"，所以它不会顺带把「攒够就蒸」推迟一个最短间隔。
- **间隔在调用之前就记下**，所以一次跑空了（没有新卡片）也算数，不会因为"没产出"而在下一分钟再问一遍。追平的批次计数同理：调用之前就 +1，失败也算用掉一个名额——上限才是真的上限。记录在库里的 `.auto-state.json`（`lastAttemptAt` / `startedAt` / `batchDay` / `batchesToday`），**重启不重置**。
- 它和 `.distill-state.json` 是两件事：后者是**游标**（哪些行已经读过），前者是**尝试时间**。混在一起会让"读过了但没产出"变得无法表达。
- 自动、按钮、`memory_distill` 共用**一把锁**：正在跑的时候，第二条路拿到的是"已经有一次在跑"，不会排队、不会两份一起花。
- 想关掉：`auto.enabled=false`（总开关），或者把规则都设 0（留着开关但没规则，等于不跑）。

readme.section: 什么时候它会自己蒸：三条规则
readme.text: 上面这张是真机：总开关开着，攒够 10 条就跑、每天补一次、两次之间至少隔 60 分钟，静默时段留空。改完点保存，下一拍就按新值判断——不用重载插件，也不用重启。

`maxEpisodesPerRun` 是**一次蒸馏最多读多少条情节**，不是一次模型调用喂多少条。插件按 `maxOutputTokens` 折算每批条数（约 320 输出 token 一条情节），一批一次调用、批批独立落盘：40 条情节是五次左右的小调用，而不是一次要 40 张卡的巨型调用。

两个原因：一是答案要装得进输出上限，二是某一批失败（限流、超时、网络断）时，前面几批的卡片已经写进库里、蒸馏游标也标好了，重跑只补剩下的。真遇到某一批仍然被截断，插件把它对半拆开重试；只剩一条还截断才是真失败，会照实报错（`maxOutputTokens` 那句话）。

`memory_distill` 的 `dryRun` 只跑第一批并报出还剩几条——预览不该把你的额度烧在整摞情节上。

**A. 跟随设置里的模型（默认）**

`transport: 'harness'` 时，插件不碰 key、不碰 endpoint，直接向 Harness 的 `llm` 服务要一次调用，用的是你在 **Settings → 模型** 里选中的那一路：提供商、模型、思考强度（thinking）全部照搬。你在设置里给模型配过 key 了，插件就不用再要第二个。

- 想换抽取用的模型？在设置里换，插件下一次蒸馏就跟上。
- 想固定一个便宜的小模型专门做抽取？把 `useCurrentModel` 关掉，填 `provider` + `model`（例如 `deepseek` / `deepseek-chat`），key 仍然是设置里那套。
- 想跑更省或更强的思考档？填 `reasoningEffort`，取值是那个模型在设置里给出的档位 id（如 `high`）；留空就沿用设置里的选择。
- 这条路上没有密钥可泄露：插件全程只报"用了哪个提供商/模型/档位"，不接触凭据值。

**B. 自己填 endpoint 直连（`http`）**

抽取器完全独立，用自己的端点、模型和额度。适合：抽取想用一个别处的小模型、想接到自建网关、或者这个 Harness 构建里没有暴露 `llm` 服务。

设置页里也有 `extractor.apiKey` 一栏（密码框，不回显已存的值），但你**最好别用它**：填进去的值会明文落进 profile 的配置里。用 `apiKeyEnv` 指个名字、把值放进环境变量或 `~/.dsh/.credentials.yaml`，是这个插件设计上的默认路线。

readme.section: http 模式的 key 从哪来
readme.text:
按这个顺序找，找到就用，一路都不写进日志、不写进审计、不写进记忆库：

1. 配置里的 `extractor.apiKey`（不推荐，会落到 YAML 里）
2. 进程环境变量 `extractor.apiKeyEnv` 指定的那个名字
3. **Harness 自己的凭据库** `~/.dsh/.credentials.yaml` 里 `refs.<apiKeyEnv>` 指向的条目

第 3 条的意思是：如果你已经把 key 配给 Harness 用（比如 `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`），把 `apiKeyEnv` 改成同名就行，不用再导出环境变量。读凭据库时只解析 `refs:` 那一段，别的内容不碰。`memory_stats` 会告诉你这次蒸馏走的是哪条路、用的哪个模型（`extractor:` 那一行），但永远只报来源、不报值。

| 工具 | 作用 |
| --- | --- |
| `memory_search` | 跨项目检索，返回 id + 摘要 + 命中原因 |
| `memory_get` | 读一张卡片的全文和关联实体 |
| `memory_timeline` | 按时间看，保留 supersede 链 |
| `memory_graph` | 从一个实体或卡片出发，看它连着哪些记忆和邻近实体 |
| `memory_remember` | 显式写一张卡片 |
| `memory_forget` | `retract` 撤回（留痕）或 `purge` 删除 |
| `memory_distill` | 用抽取模型把原始事件蒸馏成卡片 |
| `memory_stats` | 库位置、数量、上次蒸馏时间 |
| `memory_backfill` | 把**插件装上之前**的会话历史导入记忆库（可重复跑，已有轮次跳过） |

`memory_graph` 是"神经元"那部分的具体形态：边不是凭空生成的，而是**两张卡片提到同一个实体**。它不声称因果，只声称"这两个东西在同一段记忆里出现过"，模型看到之后自己判断。

**没有自动注入。** 记忆只在模型主动调用工具时才进入上下文——这是刻意的：大多数轮次根本不需要长期记忆，注入了就是纯成本。

采集只看得见**宿主开着的时候**发生的对话，所以新装的库一开始是空的——装之前的几十个会话不会自己冒出来。`memory_backfill` 补这一段：它回放磁盘上的会话文件（`~/.dsh/sessions/<项目目录>/<会话>/session.v4.jsonl.zstd`），转成和实时采集**同样格式**的情节。

- **走的还是那套过滤**：`<system-reminder>` 剥掉、运行时快照（runtime context、压缩检查点）不算人话、限长、脱敏，全部复用 `src/turns.js`——实时和回填只有一份实现，不会两边慢慢走偏。
- **时间是原来的时间**：`t` 取自会话文件里那一轮的时间戳，情节落进它**当天**的 `episodes/YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl`，不是全堆在今天。
- **可以重复跑**：一轮对话的唯一身份是 `(会话, 轮次)`，库里已经有了就跳过；所以一个还在长的会话，下次再跑只补新的部分。删档重装、换机器、插件装晚了，都是这一条命令的事。
- **默认只统计不写库**（`dryRun`），先看数字再决定。

一句话的形状：

```text
memory_backfill {dryRun: true}     → 133 个会话 / 将写入 2078 条情节
memory_backfill {dryRun: false}    → 已写入 2078 条情节；已存在跳过 85 条
```

回填出来的是**情节**，还没变成卡片：蒸馏一次（`memory_distill`、设置页按钮，或让自动蒸馏一天跑一批，默认每批 40 条）才会进检索层。2000 条情节要花的就是 50 批模型调用，这件事该由你决定什么时候花——想让它自己慢慢消化完，打开 `auto.catchUp`（追平模式）：它一天最多跑 `auto.maxBatchesPerDay` 批，追平就自己停。回填结束时会顺手把 `README.md` 和 `graph.html` 按新情节重画一次，所以打开这两个文件看到的是当下的库，不是导入前的样子。

会话文件是**拼接的 zstd 容器**（每次追加写一帧），所以读它要先把帧切开——`src/history.js` 里有一个和 harness 自己用的算法同构的帧扫描器。

- **它是立体的**：不是一张平面图，而是一团有远近的星云。拖一下云就转——背后的记忆会转到前面来，前面的会退到远处变小变暗。滚轮推进拉远，双击回到初始角度。
- **每个记忆是一颗神经元**：白热的核 + 一圈同色的光晕 + 几根会弯的树突。颜色就是 kind：决策（紫）/ 事实（青）/ 待解（洋红）/ 偏好（橙）/ 记录（绿）。
- **实体是发白的枢纽**（`infra`、`deepseek`、`blog-engine`、`memory-graph`……）：大小按被提及次数长，颜色取自它周围那张记忆的颜色，所以一个枢纽落在哪个区域一眼就能看出来。跨项目共享的实体额外带一个标记。
- **同一 kind 的记忆聚成一片**，每片外面浮着淡淡的名字（决策记忆 / 事实知识 / 偏好态度 / 记录 / 未决疑问）——那是区域名，不是节点。
- **细白线是"同一段记忆里出现过"**：短的是卡片和它的实体，横穿几片区域的那几根是长程联系。虚线 = 已被替换（`superseded`），能看见「改口」发生在哪里；撤回的卡片仍在，只是灰掉。
- 搜标题 / 实体 / id、按项目过滤、点一颗神经元看详情（它和邻居会亮起来，其余淡下去）、悬停看提示、`Esc` 清除。
- 跟随系统深浅色（深色是黑底光晕，浅色是纸面彩点）；也可以直接跳到 `#dark`、`#light`、`#still`（停止缓慢自转），或者 `#dark&<卡片id|实体slug>` 一次把主题和某颗神经元都定好。
- 每次 `memory_remember` / `memory_forget` / `memory_distill` 之后自动重画；空库和只有一张卡的库都有能读的提示，不会白屏。

浅色：

它是**一个自包含的 HTML 文件**：没有 CDN、没有 three.js、没有框架、没有构建步骤、没有网络请求，透视投影和辉光都是手写的 canvas 2D，数据是渲染时内联进去的。168 张卡片 + 332 个实体 → 459 KB。丢掉它也无所谓，下次写入会重新生成。

位置是**算出来的、可重放的**：三维力导向的初值来自卡片 key 的哈希，同样的库画两遍每一颗神经元都在同一个位置——所以两次渲染的 HTML 除了时间戳完全一致（有测试盯着这件事）。

一个明确的边界：`graph.html` 是**整个库**的静态快照，双击就开、不依赖 harness。会话里"这个会话记住了什么"是另一张图，见下一节。

readme.section: 不用找文件：侧栏里的「记忆图谱」
readme.text:
不想翻记忆库目录的话，插件在应用左侧栏注册了一个**「记忆图谱」**入口（和 插件 / 自动化任务 / 上下文洞察 同一列），点开就是上面这张整库图：

- 面板里嵌的是同一个 `graph.html`，走宿主自己的 `/api/memory-graph.page` 路由——**同一份渲染器**，不是第二套实现，所以面板里有的搜索/过滤/悬停，双击文件打开的那个也一定有，反过来也一样。
- 顶栏两个按钮：**刷新**（重画，读到刚写进去的卡片）、**新窗口打开**（拿这个页面开一个真正的浏览器窗口，图能占满屏）。
- 只读、不花钱：这条路由只读磁盘上的卡片和实体页，不写文件、不调模型。`X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN`，所以只有应用自己能把它嵌进去。
- 记忆库目录**不会**出现在浏览器里——面板拿的是路由，不是文件路径。
- 面板里的画面就是上面那两张图（同一份 HTML、同一个透视相机），只是窗口更窄：窄到侧栏那个尺寸时，云会自动缩小到刚好放得下，标签也减到六条以内，不会挤成一片。

- 中间的深色点是本次会话；从它伸出去的浅蓝点是这个会话写下的每条情节（`T1`、`T2`……）。
- **绿色虚线**是这个会话自己的话真的能唤回的卡片——用的是 `memory_search` 同一个函数，所以图上亮着的就是模型查"你还记得吗"时真会拿到的东西。
- 灰色点是实体，卡片和实体之间是"这张卡提到它"，情节和实体之间是"这一轮的话里出现了它"。
- 跨项目的卡片通过共享实体挂进来（虚线边框、暗一档）：这是实体层唯一的存在理由，所以它在图上是看得见的。
- 点任意节点，右侧展开它的全文；点空白处收起。页头有计数、项目、跨项目数、一个**蒸馏一次**按钮和一个刷新按钮；页签开着时每 20 秒静默重取一次。
- **蒸馏一次**就是手动跑那一次蒸馏：走的是 `memory_distill` 工具背后同一个 `distill()`，用你在设置里选中的模型，跑完把「读出 N 条情节 → M 张卡片」写在页头下面，随即重画图。采集是随手记；蒸馏有三条路：你按这个按钮、模型自己调 `memory_distill`、或者按下面的规则自动跑——三条路走同一把锁，永远不会同时跑两份。

右上角两个按钮：**蒸馏一次** 和 **刷新**。

点开一个情节，右侧就是那一轮你自己说的话：

前面那张是记忆库还没蒸馏过的样子——只有情节，没有卡片和实体，面板顶上那句提示就是在说这件事。按下「蒸馏一次」之后，同一个会话变成这样：紫色是卡片，灰色是实体，中间那团是本次会话，虚线是「这条记忆是在这里被说出来的」：

图上的卡片就是这个会话里蒸馏出来的东西——包括你提的那几条需求本身。

数据不是塞进页面里的：宿主注册了两条 exact Fetch route——`/api/memory-graph.graph`（GET，读这一个会话的图）和 `/api/memory-graph.distill`（POST，按一下才有、跑一次蒸馏）——harness 的 Connection 先验浏览器的签名、只放行 owner Peer，浏览器拿自己已有的 cookie 请求即可。插件里没有第二套鉴权，也没有把库目录暴露给页面；蒸馏那条只收 POST，所以刷新页面或预取都不可能顺手花掉一次模型调用。布局是在**宿主**算的（确定性力导向），浏览器只负责把坐标画出来，所以重开页签是同一张图。

上限：情节 40、卡片 60、实体 40、跨项目 12、边 420。超了页头会照实报总数，图只画最近的这些——一张图看不清的时候，它就没用了。

> 改完怎么生效：`client.js` 刷新页面就行（宿主每次请求现读这个文件）；改了宿主侧（`index.js` / `src/*.js`）要在插件管理器里把「记忆图谱」关掉再打开，它会重新 `apply`，不用重启整个应用。

同一个人的多个项目之间互相联想，不是多人共享记忆。

你在 A 项目里定过"所有脚本必须零依赖"，三个月后在 B 项目里问"这个库能不能省掉构建步骤"，`memory_search` 会把 A 项目那张卡片带出来——因为它们共享实体 `零依赖`。这就是实体层存在的唯一原因。

写入前拦截，不是写完再清：

- 内置规则：各类 API key、私钥块、`password=` 形态、Bearer token
- `redactEmails`：邮箱 → `[email]`
- `redactPaths`：家目录 → `~`
- `denyPatterns`：你自己的正则

命中即替换为 `[REDACTED]`，审计日志只记录"哪条规则触发"，**不记录命中内容**。万一有东西漏进来，`memory_forget mode=purge` 直接删文件。

Harness 会把运行时快照、技能目录、时间戳、审批通知、压缩摘要**伪装成 user 消息**投递进来。这些不是你的话，蒸馏它们只会凭空造出记忆。

所以采集看两件事，**两条都过一遍**：`source.kind`（不是 `user` 就丢）和 `capture.skipPatterns` 的文本正则。

为什么两条都要看，而不是只看来源：来源不是每次都可靠——实测库里就躺过一条 1501 字的图像工具说明，它带的正是 `kind: 'user'`，于是被当成你说的话记了下来。来源只能**增加**跳过，不能否决文本规则。

判断之前，先剥掉有边界的那种注入（`<system-reminder>…</system-reminder>`）。这样一条真的消息里带了提醒时，剥完留下的是你的原话，而不是整条被丢掉。

顺带的好处：一轮里不再被中途插入的注入消息切断，情节的边界就是真正的轮次边界。

- **不回溯**。采集只从插件在场那一刻开始（这个库里第一条情节是 2026-11-02 15:53，就是插件第一次被启用的时间）。更早的会话一条情节都没有，插件也不会去读历史会话记录——记忆从你装上它的那一刻起长。
- **子智能体会话也会被记**。我派出去干活的子智能体，它们的开场提示词会被当成一条情节（项目名按 cwd 推断）。这些是内部指令，不是你的记忆；目前没有过滤，看到就是一条噪音。

1. **实体层是跨项目的关键**。两个项目共享"同一个 Postgres 实例""同一个工具"，通过 entity 页连起来，而不是靠向量相似度碰运气。
2. **时间有效性 `[valid_from, valid_to]`**。没有它，记忆图会把三个月前的方案和昨天的方案平铺在一起，安静地撒谎。
3. **写入是情节，不是事实**。`episodes` 记"什么时候、因为什么、谁决定"；`cards` 是从情节派生的结论。
4. **遗忘是功能**。`retract` 保留痕迹，比假装没发生诚实；`purge` 才是真删。
5. **图是派生缓存**。会话日志是唯一真相源，卡片全部可以从 episodes 重新蒸馏出来。

零依赖，不联网，不碰真实记忆库：

```bash
npm test        # 43 + 13 + 35 + 12 + 22 + 54 + 15 + 8 + 11 + 25 + 12 + 27 = 277 项检查，另加 25 题检索评测
npm run eval    # 只跑检索评测（离线，确定性的）
```

- `test/smoke.mjs` — 存储、隐私过滤、BM25 检索、实体扩散、supersede 链、蒸馏结果解析；另外验证近义标题不会在图上分叉（同一张卡换了措辞 → 归一化到老卡、正文取更全的那份、不跨项目；写了 `supersedes` 的推翻不被当成重复）
- `test/schema.mjs` — 设置页和运行时不许漂移：双向比对 `Config({})` 和 `resolveConfig({})` 的每个叶子（只有 `vaultDir` 例外，页面存原始文本、运行时存绝对路径）——页面多一格没用的、少一格看不见的都算失败；另外验证 `transport` 只认那两个值、数值边界、`apiKey` 被标成 secret、volatile 叶子数量正好等于页面的字段表（多一格少一格都失败）、四个结构键不许出现在页面字段表里
- `test/client.mjs` — 把设置页挂在一个够用的 React 替身上跑：页面画出的控件 = 该显示的字段、切换 `transport` 后 http 那几项才出现、空的内联 key 不会被当成"删除"发出去、越界的数字到不了线上、宿主拒绝后清空草稿并报错、「恢复默认」发的是 `unset` 而不是 `set`、只在真的和继承值不同时才打「已自定义」（同一次保存会钉住整行，值等于默认的不算改过）、样式表只有一个带包名标记的 `<style>`、`client.js` 里不许出现 `export`/`import`（loader 按脚本求值）；再把 `client.js` 真的放进一个带 `window.__ModuleLoader__` 的假页面里求值，走一遍 factory → `apply` 的浏览器路径（只 `require('react')`、注册 id 是包名、四处 order 分别 25 / 30 / 30、标签跟随页面语言、动作栏是滚动区的兄弟而不是它里面的 sticky 子元素）；再验证**侧栏入口 + 主面板**（`sidebar.panellist` 与 `main` 用同一个 id 才连得上、面板里嵌的是那条路由而不是第二套渲染、src 里不带库路径）；最后驱动**会话页签**：只按 `sessionId` 请求 `/api/memory-graph.graph`、宿主给的节点和边一个不少地画出来、点卡片在右侧展开标题与正文、点空白收起、空会话和失败的路由都给人话
- `test/graphdata.mjs` — 会话页签的数据：按 `session` 过滤情节（别的会话一条都不带）、项目多数决、召回查询取最近几轮并截断、布局确定且不越界、每条边都指向存在的节点、跨项目卡片通过共享实体挂进来、上限与截断照实报、assistant 原文不进 payload；路由对"缺 session /

下面两个测试会真的联网/花钱，所以不在 `npm test` 里，要自己跑：

```bash
npm run live             # 真模型端到端：3 条情节 → 蒸馏 → 再检索回来
node test/live.mjs --backlog 12 --tokens 3000   # 12 条情节，看它真分成两批
node test/live.mjs --tokens 900                 # 输出上限压低，看它截断后对半拆
npm run live:supersede   # 真模型：先记一条，再让它被"更正"推翻，验证作废链

它们从 `~/.dsh/.credentials.yaml` 或环境变量取 key（见下文），不写死、不落盘。这两个脚本跑在普通 `node` 进程里，没有 Harness 的 `llm` 服务可借，所以它们显式用 `transport: 'http'`；插件自己在界面里默认走 harness。

版本号只有一个来源：`package.json` 的 `version`。发一个版本就等于打一个 tag：

```bash
npm run release        # = npm version patch（先跑测试）→ 提交 → tag → git push --follow-tags
npm version minor -m "chore(release): v%s" && git push --follow-tags   # minor / major 换这个写法
```

推上去的 tag 会触发 `.github/workflows/publish.yml`，它只做四件事：

1. 核对 tag 和 `package.json` 的版本号——不一致就失败，不会发出一个版本号对不上的包；
2. 查这个版本是不是已经在注册表上——在就跳过，重推同一个 tag 是空操作而不是报错；
3. `npm publish --provenance --access public`（`prepublishOnly` 会再跑一遍那 277 项，红的进不去）；
4. npm 页面上多一条「Built and signed on GitHub Actions」，证明这个 tarball 是从这个仓库的这个提交构建的。

凭据有两条路，工作流两条都认（有 `NPM_TOKEN` 就用它，没有就走 OIDC）：

**一、Trusted publishing——推荐，仓库里不存任何密钥。** npm 把这条当正路，同时正在把「绕过 2FA 的 token」收掉（npm 的公告：账号类操作 2026 年 8 月起限制，直接发布 2027 年 1 月起禁用）。在包页面上：**Package → Settings → Trusted publishing → Add a publisher → GitHub Actions**，repository 填 `ilaomianyang/dsh-memory-graph`，workflow 填 `publish.yml`，environment 留空。之后 CI 用这次运行的 OIDC 身份发布，`--provenance` 自动带上。

**二、`NPM_TOKEN`——今天就能用，过渡方案。** npmjs.com → Access Tokens → Generate New Token，选 **Granular Access Token**：勾上 **Bypass two-factor authentication (2FA)**，Permissions 选 **Read and write (publish and stage)**（如果出现选包的地方，只勾这一个包），Expiration 别留默认的 30 天。然后加到仓库：Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → New repository secret，名字 `NPM_TOKEN`。账号开着 2FA 时，普通的 Publish token 会被 `403 ... two-factor authentication ... required to publish` 挡回来，只有勾了 bypass 的发得出去。这个 token 只给 CI 用，别写进 `~/.npmrc`。

不想等 CI、或者 GitHub 那一刻连不上，就在本地发：

```bash
npm publish            # publishConfig 已经把 registry 钉在 npmjs，prepublishOnly 会跑测试
git push --follow-tags # 别忘推 tag，否则 CI 里没有这次发布的记录
```

手动发过之后，CI 那条会命中第 2 步的跳过分支，不会再发一次。

readme.section: 蒸馏实测（真模型跑过，不是估计）
readme.text:
用 `deepseek-chat`，`npm run live`：

| 输入 | 产出 | 耗时 | token |

| 3 条合成情节（中英混排，2 个项目） | 5 张卡片，项目归属 5/5 正确 | 2.9 s / 3.6 s（两次） | ≈1 590 |

readme.section: 蒸馏实测（真模型跑过，不是估计）
readme.text:
第一版是一次调用喂完所有待蒸馏情节。在真实记忆库上第一次跑就撞了墙：23 条情节要产出三十来张卡，3 000 输出 token 截断，整批白跑。现在按输出上限分批——**同一份后台，拆成几次小调用，反而更快也更抗失败**。

`npm run live:supersede` 验证的是**时间有效性真的会动**：第一轮记下「上传到 GitHub 共享」，第二轮用户更正「共享的是插件，不是记忆」，抽取模型自己填 `supersedes`，旧卡转 `superseded` 并写 `valid_to`，两边链接互指。这条链在离线测试里只能验证机制，验证不了模型会不会填。

顺带一个真实的教训：我第一次拿**旧快照**回放时，蒸馏出的卡片把"记忆要上传 GitHub 共享"当成了现行结论。查下来的原因不是模型错，是那份快照早于用户的更正——**记忆只能和它读到的东西一样好**。所以插件做的是：情节永远留着，卡片可被推翻（`supersedes`），推翻也可被查（`memory_timeline`）。

`eval/` 是一套离线评测：38 张卡片 / 3 个项目 / 5 种 kind / 7 个跨项目共享实体 / 4 条 supersede 链 / 1 张 retracted，25 道检索题（keyword 9、entity-bridge 6、temporal 5、negative 5）外加 4 对（8 条）「问历史 vs 问现状」成对题，跑仓库里真实的 `searchCards`，不自己写一套评分。题目是先写好的，跑完没有改过一个字。

```bash
npm run eval
```

当前结果（limit 5、hops 1）：

**[`eval/REPORT.md`](eval/REPORT.md) 里写着这份评测没覆盖什么，以及八个已知弱点**——包括「问历史」「问现状」这类意图靠一条正则判断，同样是穷举（实测 10 条变体里仍会漏）；包括「监控之前那套还留着吗」这种问现状却把老卡排第一；包括 `部署`、`流程` 这种有主题义的常见词会让 negative 的判据停在灰区。0/5 只该读作"这 5 条过了"，不该读作"负面问题修好了"；4 对成对题只有 4 对，是抛硬币级别的证据。想信这个分数之前先读那份报告。

一处刻意的设计：**问历史有单独的通路**。「抽取模型现在默认开着吗」会压制作废的旧卡、把现行结论顶上来；「最早那版抽取方案是什么」则反过来，把作废卡还原到满权重。同一批词、不同的时态，答案不是一个——降权不该等于捞不出来。

- 检索是关键词 BM25 + 实体扩散，**没有向量召回**。中英文混合场景下中文靠 bigram 分词，可用但不如嵌入模型；卡片量到几千张时应该换。
- 蒸馏质量取决于抽取模型，且**只在你显式调用时发生**，不会自己跑。建议配合定时任务。
- harness 模式借的是「设置里当前选中的那个模型」，所以你在对话里换模型，抽取也跟着换；想钉死一个抽取专用模型就把 `useCurrentModel` 关掉。另外它花的是同一个模型提供商的额度，不会因为"插件"就变免费。
- `graph.html` 是**静态 HTML**（整个库的快照）；会话页签里的「记忆」是 GUI 面板，但它只画**当前会话**那一小块，不是整库的交互图。侧栏的「记忆图谱」补上了这一块：它把整库图嵌进应用，但用的是 iframe + 那条只读路由，搜索/缩放/过滤仍然是页面自己的那套，不是 React 重画。——整库的缩放/搜索/过滤仍然在 `graph.html` 里。
- 会话页签的数据来自两条 `/api/memory-graph.*` 路由，所以它需要一个能跑 Web GUI 的环境；headless / CLI 配置下插件照常工作，只是没有这个页签。改了 `client.js` 刷新页面即可，改了宿主侧要重新 `apply`（插件管理器里关掉再打开）。
- 卡片去重先是"同项目 + 标题归一化相同"，再放宽到标题的**词面重合度 ≥ 0.55**（用的是检索那套 bigram 分词；实测无关卡片最高 0.20，同一件事换个措辞 0.60–0.78）。所以「蒸馏走独立模型接口」和「蒸馏用独立模型接口」现在是一张卡，不会在图上分叉。但**写了 `supersedes` 的卡片跳过这层判断**——「监控换成 Prometheus」和「监控换到 Uptime Kuma」词面再像也是新决定。语义相反、措辞又差得远的仍会存成两张：这层只做词面近似，不读意思。
- 设置页是四张写死的分组卡片 + 一张手写字段表，不是对 schema 的通用反射；`test/schema.mjs` 负责保证两边一致——改了 schema 却忘了改字段表，结果是测试挂掉，而不是页面上多出一个控件。`skipPatterns` / `denyPatterns` 仍然是多行文本框一行一条。
- 页面**不轮询**：配置在别处（手改 YAML、另一个窗口）被改过之后，页面要等下一次保存往返才会重读；你未保存的草稿会被保留。
- 采集粒度是一轮（`turn/end` 触发落盘），不是一条一条消息；一轮里的多次工具调用只记次数不记内容。连续多步的长轮次只留前 6 段可见文本。
- 记忆库自带 `.gitignore`（忽略 `*.tmp`、系统垃圾文件和 `.distill-state.json`）；后者是每台机器各

[](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@ilaomianyang/dsh-memory-graph) [](https://github.com/ilaomianyang/dsh-memory-graph/actions/workflows/test.yml)

Long-term **associative memory** for [DeepSeek Harness](https://getartcraft.com) (DSH).

Context compaction quietly deletes things. This plugin keeps a second layer — outside the context window, on your own disk, readable by you — so that a decision you made three months ago can still be found.

Plain Node ESM, no build step. Its configuration lives in **Settings → Memory Graph** (four groups on one page, applied on save); there are two places to look — the **Memory tab in a conversation** draws what that session remembered, graph.html at the vault root draws the whole library.

The only third-party dependency is the harness's own `@deepseek-ai/schemastery`, which supplies the config schema (the page reads the value projected from it); without it the plugin still runs and the Memory Graph page simply does not appear.

---

readme.section: How this differs from "compressing the context"
readme.text:
| | Context compaction | This plugin |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Goal | make the current conversation fit | make last quarter's decision findable |
| Loss | compressed away = gone | raw events are append-only, never rewritten |
| Structure | one paragraph of summary | typed cards with time, provenance and entity links |
| Change | invisible | conflicts become a supersede chain you can read |
| Location | inside the session log | a folder of plain files you own |

readme.section: How this differs from "compressing the context"
readme.text: Compaction is a **working-memory** strategy. This is **long-term memory**. They coexist; neither replaces the other.

```
episodes/   raw      one JSON line per turn, never distilled, never deleted
cards/      semantic typed memory cards distilled from the raw layer (markdown)
entities/   index    one page per thing, with a timeline of mentions
```

Retrieval reads `cards + entities`. `episodes` is the raw material for distillation, and the audit trail when something looks wrong.

```markdown
---
id: "c-20261102-7f3a"
kind: "decision"
title: "Store memories as plain text instead of SQLite"

`status` is only ever `active`, `superseded` or `retracted`. **A belief that was overturned is never deleted** — it becomes `superseded` and points at the card that replaced it. That is what makes "how did this come to be" readable.

**From npm** (no GitHub involved):

```
plugin_manager action=install_bundle target="@ilaomianyang/dsh-memory-graph"
```

pnpm pulls in the one dependency, `@deepseek-ai/schemastery`, with it. If that is slow where you are, pass `registry="https://registry.npmmirror.com/"` — npmmirror mirrors npm automatically, usually minutes to hours behind a publish.

**From source** (when you want to follow the code):

```
git clone https://github.com/ilaomianyang/dsh-memory-graph
cd dsh-memory-graph
npm install                 # one dependency: the harness's own schema library
```

Then, in Harness, let the model run this, or point the plugin manager at that directory:

```
plugin_manager action=install_bundle target="<absolute path of the clone>"
```

That path links a local directory with `link:`, which does **not** install the package's dependencies, so do not skip `npm install` above. Without it the plugin still runs — there is simply no Memory Graph page in Settings.

To follow along: `git pull`, then reload the plugin (`plugin_manager action=set_plugin target="include:memory-graph" enabled=false`, then `enabled=true`).

The vault defaults to `~/dsh-memory` and is created on activation.

**Restart Harness once after installing** (close the window and reopen it). Not out of laziness: the web-side plugin manifest is composed by scanning the running loader's entries at startup and reading each package's `dsh.client` field, and that scan is cached in the process — it is never repeated. So a fresh install, or any edit to `client.js` or `package.json`, needs a new process; install without restarting and the sidebar simply has no Memory Graph entry, with no error anywhere to tell you why.

After the restart it is **Settings → Memory Graph**, between Models and Plugins.

Uninstall with `plugin_manager action=remove_bundle target="@ilaomianyang/dsh-memory-graph"`. The vault is not touched — it lives in `~/dsh-memory`, independent of the plugin.

The copy installed from npm gets a **Version & updates** row at the top of its Settings page: the version you are running, **Check**, and **Update**.

That is the real page (on a development machine the install is a `link:`, so Update is greyed out and says why next to it): the version, whether it is current, which registry, when it last checked — and the four `update.*` switches below.

- It checks once at startup, then at most every `update.checkEveryHours` hours (default 12). The request is one `GET` of `<registry>/@ilaomianyang%2fdsh-memory-graph/latest` — no query string, no vault path, no conversation content. The answer is cached in the vault's `.update-state.json`, so an offline machine keeps the last answer instead of showing "could not check" as "up to date".
- Nothing is installed until you press Update. Installation goes through the host's own `pluginManager.installBundle` — the same path `dsh plugin` and the plugin manager use — so it respects your configured registry instead of inventing a second package manager.
- **A `link:` install is refused**, and the refusal is a sentence rather than an error: "updating would overwrite your working copy". For a clone, updating is `git pull` and a reload, as above.
- An install usually needs a Harness restart (same caching reason as `client.js` / `package.json`). The page says **restart Harness to apply** rather than pretending it is already running the new code.
- `update.autoInstall` (off by default) installs a newer version at startup without being asked. It acts before any conversation starts, which is the on
Turn `update.enabled` off to stop it going online entirely: after that it sends nothing, and the page only shows the current version.

├── vault.json                   schema version, creation time
├── projects.json                project slugs seen so far

One file is one memory. Append-only. No binaries, no lockfiles. Run `git init` inside it if you want version history, or `grep -r` the whole vault.

**This is your private local data.** What gets shared on GitHub is the plugin, not the vault.

**Settings → Memory Graph.** The plugin contributes its own page to the Settings sidebar, four groups: capture / privacy / extractor / retrieval. Every field carries a bilingual description and applies the moment you press Save — no restart, no reload.

- A field you changed is badged as changed; the restore link next to it goes back to the default rather than blanking the value.
- A rejected save says why (a number out of range, a host that was changed elsewhere in the meantime) instead of swallowing the edit.
- The extractor group follows the route you pick: `harness` shows only the model knobs, `http` reveals the endpoint and key.

readme.section: When it distils on its own: three rules
readme.text:
By default it does **not**. With `auto.enabled` on, the plugin looks once a minute at whether a run is due — and that look is arithmetic only (how many episodes are waiting, how long since the last attempt, is this a quiet hour). **No model call, no cost.** Only a rule that matches starts a run, and it runs the same `distill()`.

The three rules are independent: any one alone, or all of them.

readme.section: When it distils on its own: three rules
readme.text:
| Rule | Setting | Fires when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Distil once enough pile up | `auto.minEpisodes` | undistilled episodes ≥ this number (say 10) |
| Distil on a schedule | `auto.everyMinutes` | this many minutes have passed since the last automatic run (1440 = daily) |
| Catch up | `auto.catchUp` | a **full batch** is still waiting (≥ `maxEpisodesPerRun`): run batch after batch, `auto.catchUpEveryMinutes` apart (default 10), at most `auto.maxBatchesPerDay` batches a day (default 6, 0 lifts the cap) |

readme.section: When it distils on its own: three rules
readme.text: Catch-up is for a **backlog** — an imported history, a week away from the machine, two thousand undistilled episodes. The other two rules digest one batch per trigger and would take dozens of days; catch-up keeps going until less than a batch is left, then goes quiet.

readme.section: When it distils on its own: three rules
readme.text:
- It has **its own cadence** (`catchUpEveryMinutes`) and is not held back by `minGapMinutes`; the other two rules still are.
- `maxBatchesPerDay` is the only knob that puts a **ceiling on automatic spending**: the default six batches is about 240 episodes a day. Raise it to drain faster, or set `quietHours` so it does not run at night.
- An interrupted catch-up (restart, shutdown, another run holding the lock) loses nothing: the counter lives in `.auto-state.json`, the next interval continues, and nothing already distilled is distilled twice.
- 2080 episodes at the defaults: six batches a day × 40 episodes ≈ nine days. Set the cap to 50 to finish in a day.

readme.section: When it distils on its own: three rules
readme.text:
- `auto.minGapMinutes` (default 30): the two **non-catch-up** rules never fire closer than this. It is checked before them — a vault that just crossed the threshold should not be asked again a minute later, and every ask costs money.
- `auto.quietHours` (default empty): nothing runs inside this window; it may cross midnight (`23:00-08:00`). Unreadable text is ignored rather than silencing the feature forever. Catch-up obeys it too.
- `auto.project` (default empty): which project automatic cards are filed under; empty uses the newest episode's project.

readme.section: When it distils on its own: three rules
readme.text:
- **The schedule clock starts when you switch it on**: it does not run on the spot — a daily schedule should not spend the moment you flip the switch. That clock is stored separately (`startedAt`) and is not treated as "the last run", so it does not push the threshold rule back by one minimum gap either.
- **The gap is armed before the call**, so a run that produced nothing still counts and will not be re-asked the next minute. The catch-up counter works the same way: it is incremented before the call, so a failed batch still spends its slot and the daily cap stays a real cap. Both live in `.auto-state.json` in the vault (`lastAttemptAt`, `startedAt`, `batchDay`, `batchesToday`), so **a restart does not reset them**.
- That file is not `.distill-state.json`: the latter is the **cursor** (which lines have been read), the former is the **attempt clock**. Merging them would make "read, but produced nothing" impossible to express.
- Automatic runs, the button and `memory_distill` share **one lock**: while a run is in flight, the other callers are told so rather than queued, so two of them can never spend at once.
- To stop it: `auto.enabled = false` (master switch), or set the rules to

readme.section: When it distils on its own: three rules
readme.text: That is the real thing: master switch on, run once 10 episodes are waiting, top up daily, never closer than 60 minutes apart, quiet hours empty. Save it and the very next tick decides on the new values — no remount, no restart.

`maxEpisodesPerRun` is how many episodes **one distillation** may read, not how many go into one model call. The plugin derives the batch size from `maxOutputTokens` (roughly 320 output tokens per episode), one call per batch, each batch committed before the next: forty episodes become five small calls instead of one request asked to produce forty cards.

Two reasons. The answer has to fit the output budget; and when one batch fails (rate limit, timeout, dropped connection) the cards from the earlier ones are already written and the distillation cursor already moved, so a re-run only picks up the rest. If a batch is still truncated anyway, the plugin halves it and retries — a single episode that overflows is the only real failure, and it is reported as such (the `maxOutputTokens` message).
`memory_distill` with `dryRun` previews the first batch only and says how many episodes are left: a preview should not spend your budget on the whole backlog.

readme.section: Two ways to hook up the extractor
readme.text:
**A. Borrow the model from Settings (the default)**

With `transport: 'harness'` the plugin touches no key and no endpoint: it asks the harness `llm` service for one call and gets exactly what you selected in **Settings → Models** — provider, model, and thinking level. The key is already configured there, so the plugin never needs a second one.

readme.section: Two ways to hook up the extractor
readme.text:
- Want a different extraction model? Change it in Settings; the next distillation follows.
- Want to pin a cheap small model to extraction? Turn `useCurrentModel` off and fill in `provider` + `model` (e.g. `deepseek` / `deepseek-chat`); the key still comes from Settings.
- Want a cheaper or stronger thinking level? Set `reasoningEffort` to one of the ids that model offers in Settings (e.g. `high`); leave it empty to reuse your selection.
- No secret can leak on this route: the plugin reports only the provider / model / effort it used, never a credential value.

readme.section: Two ways to hook up the extractor
readme.text:
**B. Your own endpoint (`http`)**

The extractor is fully independent: its own endpoint, model, and budget. Use it when extraction should run on a model configured elsewhere, behind your own gateway, or when this harness build exposes no `llm` service.

readme.section: Two ways to hook up the extractor
readme.text: The settings page also has an `extractor.apiKey` field (a password input that never echoes what you saved), but **do not use it**: whatever you type there is written in plaintext into the profile config. Pointing `apiKeyEnv` at a name and keeping the value in the environment or `~/.dsh/.credentials.yaml` is the intended route.

readme.section: Where the key comes from (http mode)
readme.text:
Tried in this order; whichever answers is used, and the value is never logged, never audited, never written into the vault:

1. `extractor.apiKey` in the config (not recommended — it ends up in YAML)
2. the process environment variable named by `extractor.apiKeyEnv`
3. **the harness's own credential store**: `refs.<apiKeyEnv>` in `~/.dsh/.credentials.yaml`

readme.section: Where the key comes from (http mode)
readme.text: Point 3 means that if the key is already configured for the harness (`DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`, say), you just set `apiKeyEnv` to the same name instead of exporting anything. Reading the store parses the `refs:` block only and touches nothing else. `memory_stats` prints an `extractor:` line naming the route and model it would use — never the value.

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `memory_search` | cross-project retrieval: id, snippet, and why it matched |
| `memory_get` | one card in full, plus its entities |
| `memory_timeline` | chronological view that keeps the supersede chain visible |
| `memory_graph` | walk from an entity or a card to connected memories and neighbouring entities |
| `memory_remember` | write a card explicitly |
| `memory_forget` | `retract` (keeps the trace) or `purge` (deletes the file) |
| `memory_distill` | turn raw episodes into cards with the extractor model |
| `memory_stats` | vault location, counts, last distillation |
| `memory_backfill` | import the sessions from **before the plugin was installed** (re-runnable; known turns are skipped) |

`memory_graph` is the "neuron" part made concrete: an edge is not invented, it is **two cards mentioning the same entity**. It claims co-mention, never causation — the model decides what that means.

**Nothing is injected automatically.** Memory only enters the context when the model asks for it. Most turns do not need long-term memory, and injecting it would be pure cost.

Capture only sees conversations that happen **while the host is running**, so a freshly installed vault starts empty: the dozens of sessions before it will never appear on their own. `memory_backfill` fills that gap by replaying the session files on disk (`~/.dsh/sessions/<project>/<session>/session.v4.jsonl.zstd`) into episodes of **the same shape** live capture writes.

- **Same filter, one implementation**: `<system-reminder>` blocks stripped, runtime snapshots (runtime context, compaction checkpoints) never counted as something a person said, length caps, redaction — all shared with live capture through `src/turns.js`, so the two paths cannot quietly diverge.
- **The original timestamp**: `t` comes from the turn in the log, and the episode lands in **its own** `episodes/YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl` rather than piling up under today.
- **Safe to run twice**: a turn is identified by `(session, turn)` and skipped when the vault already has it, so re-running after a session grew imports only the new part. Reinstalls, new machines and late installs are all the same command.
- **Dry run by default** (`dryRun`): see the numbers before anything is written.

In one line:

```text
memory_backfill {dryRun: true}     → 133 sessions scanned / 2078 episodes would be written
memory_backfill {dryRun: false}    → 2078 episodes written; 85 already present, skipped
```

What lands is **episodes**, not cards: distil once (`memory_distill`, the Settings button, or the daily auto run at 40 episodes a batch) and they enter the retrieval layer. Two thousand episodes is fifty model batches — that is a spend worth deciding on deliberately, and if you would rather have it drain itself, switch on `auto.catchUp`: it runs at most `auto.maxBatchesPerDay` batches a day and stops when it has caught up. A backfill also re-renders `README.md` and `graph.html` when it finishes, so those two files show the vault as it is now rather than as it was before the import.

A session file is a **concatenated zstd container** (one frame per appended batch), so reading it means cutting it frame by frame — `src/history.js` carries a scanner equivalent to the one the harness itself uses.
`memory_stats` tells you where the vault is; in its root there is also **`graph.html`** — double-click it, nothing to install, no server:

- **It is three-dimensional**: not a flat chart but a nebula with depth. Drag and the cloud turns — memories behind come forward, the ones in front recede and shrink. Scroll to push in, double-click to go back to the starting angle.
- **Every memory is a neuron**: a white-hot core, a halo in its own colour, a few curved dendrites. The colour is the kind: decision (violet) / fact (teal) / open question (magenta) / preference (amber) / note (green).
- **Entities are the paler hubs** (`infra`, `deepseek`, `blog-engine`, `memory-graph`…), sized by how often they are mentioned. A hub takes its colour from the memories around it, so you can see at a glance which region it belongs to; the cross-project ones carry an extra mark.
- **Memories of one kind gather into a region**, and each region floats its own faint name (decisions / facts / preferences / notes / open questions) — that is a place, not a node.
- **Hairlines mean "they showed up in the same memory"**: the short ones tie a card to its entity, the few long ones cross whole regions. Dashed = replaced (`superseded`), so you can see where the record changed its mind; retracted cards stay visible, greyed out.
- Search by title / enti

Light:

It is **one self-contained HTML file**: no CDN, no three.js, no framework, no build step, no network requests — the perspective projection and the glow are hand-written canvas 2D, and the data is inlined at render time. 168 cards + 332 entities → 459 KB. Delete it if you like; the next write regenerates it.

Positions are **computed and replayable**: the 3D force layout is seeded from a hash of each card key, so drawing the same vault twice puts every neuron in the same place — two renders of one vault differ only in the timestamp (there is a test watching that).

One honest limit: `graph.html` is a **static snapshot of the whole vault** — double-click it, no harness needed. "What did *this* conversation remember?" is a different picture, and it lives in the GUI: see the next section.

readme.section: Or skip the file: the Memory Graph entry in the sidebar
readme.text: If you would rather not go looking through the vault folder, the plugin registers a **Memory Graph** entry in the app's left rail (the same column as Plugins / Automations / Context insights). Click it and the whole-vault graph is right there:

readme.section: Or skip the file: the Memory Graph entry in the sidebar
readme.text:
- What the panel embeds is the same `graph.html`, served by the host over its own `/api/memory-graph.page` route — **one renderer**, not a second implementation. Whatever search, filtering and hover the panel has, the file you double-click has too, and the other way round.
- Two buttons in the bar: **Refresh** (redraw, picking up cards written a moment ago) and **Open in a window** (the same page in a real browser window, where the graph gets the whole screen).
- Read-only and free: the route reads cards and entity pages off disk. It writes nothing and calls no model. `X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN`, so only the app itself can frame it.
- The vault directory **never** reaches the browser — the panel fetches a route, not a file path.
- What you see there is the picture above (same HTML, same perspective camera), only in a narrower window: at sidebar size the cloud shrinks to fit and the labels drop to six or fewer, so nothing turns into porridge.

- The dark node in the middle is the session. The pale blue nodes around it are the episodes it wrote (`T1`, `T2`, …).
- **Green dashed edges** are the cards this session's own words would actually retrieve — computed with the same `searchCards` the model calls, so what is lit here is what the model really gets when it asks "do you remember?".
- Grey nodes are entities: a card and an entity are joined when the card mentions it, an episode and an entity when that turn named it.
- A card from another project arrives through a shared entity (dashed outline, one shade dimmer). That is the only reason the entity layer exists, so it is visible on the graph.
- Click any node and the side panel opens its full text; click the empty canvas to close it. The header carries the counts, the project, the cross-project count and a refresh button, and the tab re-reads quietly every 20 seconds while it is open.

Click an episode and the side panel shows what you actually said that turn:

readme.section: Cross-project means one person's projects, not shared memory
readme.text:
You set "every script must be zero-dependency" in project A. Three months later, in project B, you ask whether a build step can be dropped — `memory_search` surfaces the card from A, because both mention the entity `zero-dependency`.

That is the only reason the entity layer exists.

Enforced **before** the write, not cleaned up afterwards:

- built-in rules: API keys, private-key blocks, `password=` forms, Bearer tokens
- `redactEmails`: addresses become `[email]`
- `redactPaths`: your home directory becomes `~`
- `denyPatterns`: your own regexes

Matches become `[REDACTED]`. The audit log records **which rule fired, never the matched text**. If something slips in anyway, `memory_forget mode=purge` deletes the file.

The harness delivers runtime snapshots, skill catalogs, sampled timestamps, approval notices and compaction checkpoints **disguised as user messages**. Those are not your words, and distilling them would manufacture memories out of nothing.

So capture checks **both**, and both must pass: `source.kind` (anything but `user` is dropped) and the `capture.skipPatterns` text rules.

Why both, rather than provenance alone: provenance is not always right — a 1501-character image-tool briefing once sat in a real vault tagged `kind: 'user'`, and was stored as if the person had typed it. Provenance may only *add* a skip; it cannot veto the patterns.

Delimited injections (`<system-reminder>…</system-reminder>`) are stripped before that decision, so a real message that carried one keeps what the person typed instead of being dropped whole.
Side benefit: an injected message no longer cuts a turn in half, so an episode's boundary is the real turn boundary.

- **No backfill.** Capture starts the moment the plugin is present (the first episode in this vault is 2026-11-02 15:53, when it was first loaded). Older sessions have no episodes, and the plugin does not read historical session logs — memory grows from the moment you install it.
- **Subagent sessions are captured too.** A subagent's opening prompt is stored as one episode (its project inferred from the cwd). Those are internal instructions, not your memories; there is no filter for them yet, so it shows up as one line of noise.

1. **The entity layer is what makes cross-project work.** Two projects sharing "the same Postgres instance" or "the same tool" connect through an entity page, instead of hoping a vector similarity finds it.
2. **Temporal validity `[valid_from, valid_to]`.** Without it the graph lays this quarter's plan next to last quarter's and lies to you quietly.
3. **The write unit is an episode, not a fact.** `episodes` records when, why and who decided; `cards` are conclusions derived from episodes.
4. **Forgetting is a feature.** `retract` keeps the trace, which is more honest than pretending it never happened; `purge` is the real delete.
5. **The graph is a derived cache.** The session log is the source of truth; every card can be re-distilled from episodes.

No network, no real vault:

```bash
npm test        # 43 + 13 + 35 + 12 + 22 + 54 + 15 + 8 + 11 + 25 + 12 + 27 = 277 checks, plus the 25-question retrieval eval
npm run eval    # retrieval eval only (offline, deterministic)
```

- `test/smoke.mjs` — storage, redaction, BM25 retrieval, entity expansion, supersede chain, extractor parsing; and near-duplicate titles not forking the graph (a re-worded card folds into the old one, the fuller body wins, never across projects, and a card that names its `supersedes` is a reversal rather than a duplicate)
- `test/schema.mjs` — the Settings page must not drift from the runtime: every leaf of `Config({})` is compared with `resolveConfig({})` in both directions (`vaultDir` is the one exception — the page holds raw text, the runtime an absolute path), so a dead control and an invisible setting both fail; plus the transport union, numeric bounds, the `secret` role on the inline key, the volatile leaves matching the page's field table exactly, and the four structural keys staying off it
- `test/client.mjs` — mounts the page on a minimal React stand-in: the controls drawn equal the fields that should show, switching `transport` reveals the http knobs, an empty inline key is never sent as a deletion, an out-of-range number never reaches the wire, a refused save clears the drafts and explains itself, restore sends `unset` rather than `set`, a value that merely repeats the i

Two suites do touch the network (and cost money), so they are not in `npm test`:

```bash
npm run live             # real model, end to end: 3 episodes → distill → search them back
npm run live:supersede   # real model: record a decision, then correct it, check the supersede chain
node test/live.mjs --backlog 12 --tokens 3000   # 12 episodes, watch it really split into two batches
node test/live.mjs --tokens 900                 # a small output cap, watch a truncation split in half

They read the key from `~/.dsh/.credentials.yaml` or the environment (see above); nothing is hard-coded or persisted. Both run in a plain `node` process with no harness `llm` service to borrow, so they set `transport: 'http'` explicitly — the plugin's own default is `harness`.

There is one source of truth for the version: `version` in `package.json`. Releasing a version *is* pushing a tag:

```bash
npm run release        # = npm version patch (runs the suite first) → commit → tag → git push --follow-tags
npm version minor -m "chore(release): v%s" && git push --follow-tags   # for minor / major
```

The tag triggers `.github/workflows/publish.yml`, which does four things:
Two ways to authenticate; the workflow accepts both (it uses `NPM_TOKEN` when the secret exists and falls back to OIDC when it does not):

**1. Trusted publishing — recommended, no secret stored anywhere.** npm treats this as the intended path and is retiring 2FA-bypassing tokens for it (per npm's notice: account changes restricted from Aug 2026, direct publishing from Jan 2027). On the package page: **Package → Settings → Trusted publishing → Add a publisher → GitHub Actions**, repository `ilaomianyang/dsh-memory-graph`, workflow `publish.yml`, environment empty. CI then publishes as this run's OIDC identity and `--provenance` comes along for free.

**2. `NPM_TOKEN` — works today, a stopgap.** npmjs.com → Access Tokens → Generate New Token, choose **Granular Access Token**: tick **Bypass two-factor authentication (2FA)**, set Permissions to **Read and write (publish and stage)** (if it offers a package picker, pick only this package), and do not leave the Expiration at the default 30 days. Then add it to the repository: Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → New repository secret, named `NPM_TOKEN`. With 2FA on the account an ordinary Publish token is rejected with `403 ... two-factor authentication ... required to publish`; only the bypass one gets through. That token is for CI only — keep it out of `~/.npmrc`.

To publish locally instead (no CI, or GitHub is unreachable that minute):

```bash
npm publish            # publishConfig pins the registry to npmjs; prepublishOnly runs the tests
git push --follow-tags # push the tag too, or CI has no record of this release
```

After a manual publish, the CI path hits the skip branch in step 2 and will not publish twice.

| Input | Output | Time | Tokens |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 3 synthetic episodes (mixed zh/en, 2 projects) | 5 cards, project attribution 5/5 correct | 2.9 s / 3.6 s (two runs) | ≈1,590 |
| a real 266-event session log → 2 captured episodes (1,501 + 278 chars) | 9 cards (8 decision + 1 preference), Chinese in, Chinese out | 5.9 s | 2,816 (prompt 1,795 / completion 1,021) |
| 12 episodes (one conversation repeated four times, to force duplicates) | 2 batches (9 + 3) → 4 cards, the second batch entirely re-confirmations | 5.9 s | 4,153 (prompt 3,114 / completion 1,039) |

The first version fed every pending episode into a single call. Its first run against a real vault hit the wall: 23 episodes wanted thirty-odd cards, 3,000 output tokens cut the answer off, and the whole run was wasted. Now it batches by the output budget — **the same backlog, as several small calls, is both faster and harder to break**.

`npm run live:supersede` checks that temporal validity actually moves: round one records "share it on GitHub", round two the user corrects "the *plugin* is shared, not the memories"; the extractor fills `supersedes` itself, the old card flips to `superseded` with a `valid_to`, and the two link to each other. Offline tests can prove the mechanism, not that a model will use it.

One honest lesson from doing this: replaying an **older snapshot** produced a card stating "memories are meant to be shared on GitHub" as the current truth. The model was not at fault — the snapshot predated the correction. **A memory is only as good as what it read.** So episodes are kept forever, cards can be overturned (`supersedes`), and the overturning stays visible (`memory_timeline`).

`eval/` is an offline benchmark: 38 cards / 3 projects / 5 kinds / 7 cross-project entities / 4 supersede chains / 1 retracted card, 25 retrieval questions (9 keyword, 6 entity-bridge, 5 temporal, 5 negative) plus 4 paired "ask about the past vs ask about now" questions. It runs the real `searchCards` from this repo rather than a second scoring implementation. The questions were written before any number was seen and not edited afterwards.

```bash
npm run eval
```

Current result (limit 5, hops 1):

| Type | n | recall@1 | recall@5 | MRR |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| keyword | 9 | 1.00 | 1.00 | 1.00 |
| entity-bridge | 6 | 0.67 | 0.94 | 0.83 |
| temporal | 5 | 0.60 | 1.00 | 0.80 |
| history pairs (retired vs successor) | 4 | — | — | 4/4 |
| negative (not in the vault) | 5 | — | — | 0/5 false positives |
| all | 25 | 0.80 | **0.98** | 0.90 |

**[`eval/REPORT.md`](eval/REPORT.md) records what this benchmark does not cover** and lists eight known weaknesses — including that history-vs-current intent is detected by one regex (also an enumeration; it still misses some phrasings), that "is that old Kuma setup still around?" is a present-tense question the reader may treat as history, and that ordinary topic words like "deployment" keep the false-positive line fuzzy. Read that report before trusting the number: 0/5 means "these five passed", not "negatives are solved", and 4 pairs is coin-flip-grade evidence.

One deliberate asymmetry: **asking about the past gets its own path**. "Is the extractor on by default now?" demotes the retired card and promotes the current answer; "what was the first version of the extraction design?" restores the retired card to full weight. Same words, different tense, different right answer — demotion must not mean unreachable.

- Retrieval is BM25 plus entity expansion — **no vector recall**. Chinese uses bigram tokenization, which works but trails embeddings; swap it out once you pass a few thousand cards.
- Distillation quality depends on the extractor model and **only happens when you call it**. Pair it with a scheduled task.
- Harness mode borrows "whatever model is currently selected in Settings", so switching models mid-conversation also switches the extractor; turn `useCurrentModel` off to pin one. It spends that provider's quota — being a plugin does not make the calls free.
- `graph.html` is a **static HTML file** (a snapshot of the whole vault). The Memory tab in a conversation is a real GUI panel, but it draws only the **current session**. The sidebar Memory Graph closes that gap by embedding the whole-vault page itself over a read-only route — search, zoom and filtering are still the page's own, not a React redraw.
- The Memory tab reads two routes, `/api/memory-graph.*`, so it needs an environment that runs the Web GUI; in a headless or CLI profile the plugin works as usual and simply has no tab. Editing `client.js` needs only a page refresh; editing the host side needs the plugin to re-`appl
